idiom_name: net/http Request/Response (Header map + Body io.ReadCloser); gRPC proto.Message with metadata.MD
implementation_notes: net/http models the package in the standard library: Request.Header is a map-like Header (map[string][]string with canonicalized keys and multi-valued fields) while Body is a non-nil io.ReadCloser that returns EOF immediately when the message has no payload, so the transport parses headers and streams the body without ever interpreting it. The response type carries the same split (status metadata plus body), and middleware and reverse proxies rewrite headers without touching payloads. For broker-shaped boundaries the identical shape appears as a gRPC generated proto message (body) plus metadata.MD (headers); a hand-written struct with a header map and a []byte payload is the fallback when no framework type fits.
pitfalls: Body is a single-use stream: hand it to exactly one consumer, and to read it twice copy it into memory (and restore or replace r.Body) instead of reading the original again.
Always close it (defer r.Body.Close()) - leaked ReadClosers in a long-lived server leak connections and file descriptors.
Header map keys are canonicalized (textproto.CanonicalMIMEHeaderKey); writing the map directly bypasses canonicalization and produces two spellings of the same header that Get may not find.
